newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain export commitments up on last year.
newsitem.headline: EU grain export commitments up on last year.

text.p: European Union grain export commitments between July 1 and December 3 were 6.5 percent above their year-ago level, mostly as a result of higher flour and barley sales, member country officials said on Monday.
Latest figures, based on delivered export certificates, showed grain exports at 12.853 million tonnes against 12.069 million.
Flour export commitments reached 2.870 million tonnes, up from 2.773 million in the same period last year.
Commercial barley exports jumped to 2.785 million tonnes from 1.137 million in the same period last year, helped by sales to Saudi Arabia.
Commercial wheat exports, however, were still lagging on last year at 3.997 million tonnes against 4.121 million.
Malt exports fell to 1.796 million tonnes from 2.179 million.
Commercial oats commitments reached 205,000 tonnes against 29,000 during the same period last year.
Since December 3, the EU has granted 429,300 tonnes of soft wheat, 250,529 of barley, 53,842 of rye, 5,500 of oats and 3,400 tonnes of durum wheat exports through its weekly grain tender system.
